problem: For the function $f(x,y)=\frac{x}{y+\operatorname{sin}⁡x},$ evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ at the point $(0,2).$

examples.problem: For the function $f(x,y) = \dfrac{4x-y}{x+y^2},$ evaluate $\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial x}$ at the point $(2,-1).$
examples.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the quotient rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{4x-y}{x+{y}^{2}}) & =\frac{\frac{∂}{∂x}(4x-y)\cdot (x+{y}^{2})-(4x-y)\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x+{y}^{2})}{{(x+{y}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4\cdot (x+{y}^{2})-(4x-y)\cdot 1}{{(x+{y}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4x+4{y}^{2}-4x+y}{{(x+{y}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4{y}^{2}+y}{{(x+{y}^{2})}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(2,-1)\mathbin{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}{|}_{(2,-1)} & =\frac{4(-1)^{2}+(-1)}{{(2+{(-1)}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{4-1}{{3}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the sum and constant multiple rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-x{y}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{y}^{3}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-{y}^{3}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x)\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we use the product rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-{y}^{3}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x) & =(\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{4})\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x+{x}^{4}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x))-{y}^{3}\cdot (1) \\  & =((4{x}^{3})\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x+{x}^{4}\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡x))-{y}^{3} \\  & =4{x}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x-{x}^{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-{y}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$
